title: What If the 1811 New Madrid Earthquakes Hit Today?

scenes.text: What if the 1811 New Madrid earthquakes hit today? Back then, the Mississippi River ran backwards.
Three huge quakes struck the middle of America between December 1811 and February 1812, each roughly magnitude 7 to 7.7.
The first was felt across about 5 million square kilometers. Church bells reportedly rang in Boston, 1,600 kilometers away.
The last one lifted the riverbed. The Mississippi backed up and flowed backward for several hours, and temporary waterfalls formed.
Land sank and flooded to form Reelfoot Lake, about 28 kilometers long. The region was thinly populated, so the death toll is unknown.
Today about 11 million people live in the highest-risk area. FEMA estimates a repeat could cause nearly 300 billion dollars in losses.

description:
What if the New Madrid earthquakes of 1811 and 1812 hit today?
Three quakes shook the middle of America, and the Mississippi flowed backward for hours.
